Question
========
Consider the following piece of JSON:

```
[
  "Striesen Niederwaldplatz",
  "Löbtau Süd",
  "Mohorner Str."
]
```

Which statement correctly describes the syntax of a JSON array such as this one?

Answerlist
----------
* An array is wrapped in square brackets and contains zero or more values, separated by commas.
* An array is wrapped in curly brackets and contains name-value pairs, just like an object.
* An array must contain values of exactly the same type, so mixing strings and numbers is invalid.
* An array is only allowed to appear as the outermost structure of a JSON text, never nested inside an object.


Solution
========
An array is delimited by a pair of square brackets `[ ]` and simply holds zero or more values, one after another, separated by commas - there are no names involved, unlike in an object. JSON does not require the values inside an array to share the same type; a single array can freely mix strings, numbers, objects, or even other arrays. Arrays can also appear anywhere a value is expected, including nested inside an object as the value of some name.

Answerlist
----------
* True
* False
* False
* False
